title: Ethiopian Biology University Entrance Exam 2015
description: Ethiopian Biology University Entrance Exam 2015 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.
options: Professor Yalemteshay Mekonnen
Professor Sebsebe Demissew
Professor Tilahun Yilma
Professor Beyene Petros
questions.explanation: Professor Tilahun Yilma developed the vaccine for rinderpest, a viral disease that affects cattle and other cloven-hoofed animals.

questions.questionText: A grade nine student has planned to study animal cells using a compound light microscope. She prepared a slide of stained human cheek cells for this purpose. Which one of the following activities should she first do?
options: Set up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place.
Adjust the iris diaphragm until the maximum brightness is coming.
Looking through the eyepiece lens to move the objectives down.
Using coarse focusing knob to rotate the nosepiece for a higher magnification lens.
questions.explanation: When using a microscope, the correct first step is to start with the lowest power objective lens to easily locate the specimen before increasing magnification.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have
options: Lysosomes which contain hydrolytic enzymes.
Vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.
Cell wall which gives support and strength to the cell.
Chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support and strength.

questions.questionText: A plant cell is placed in a solution which has lower solute concentration than its contents. After a few minutes the cell will become
options: Flaccid
Turgid
Burst
Plasmolysed
questions.explanation: When a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis, making it turgid.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about human food digestion?
options: Mouth use protease enzyme to breakdown proteins.
The stomach physically breaks down the ingested food.
The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
Large intestine is the site of lipid hydrolysis.
questions.explanation: The small intestine is responsible for the absorption of nutrients after digestion, including amino acids, sugars, and fatty acids.

questions.questionText: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched to the food stuff it acts on?
options: Maltase - lipids
Pepsin - protein
Trypsin - starch
Amylase - fats
questions.explanation:
Pepsin is a digestive enzyme found in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.
 Maltase acts on maltose (a sugar), trypsin acts on proteins, and amylase acts on starch, not fats.

questions.questionText: Which of the following breathing movements happens when air enters into and exits from the balloon lungs in the bell-jar model?
options: Air enters when the rubber sheet is pushed up.
Air enters when the bell-jar thorax contracts.
Air exits when the balloon lungs have higher pressure than the external environment.
Air exits when Y-piece is rotated both clockwise and counterclockwise.
questions.explanation: In the bell-jar lung model, air enters the balloons (lungs) when the rubber sheet (diaphragm) is pulled down, creating low pressure inside. Air exits when the lungs have higher pressure than the external environment, causing exhalation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following structures of the heart is correctly matched with its function?
options: Left ventricle - contracts and forces oxygenated blood around the body
Right atrium - contracts and forces deoxygenated blood into the lungs
Left atrium - contracts and forces blood into the right ventricles
Right ventricle - contracts and forces blood into the left ventricles
questions.explanation:
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the rest of the body.
 The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, not to the left ventricle.

questions.questionText: Suppose your friend fails suddenly due to heart attack while he is playing football. The victim needs artificial breathing to keep him alive until medical support arrives. Which activity is strictly prohibited in this situation?
options: Open the airway by removing any obstacles from the mouth
Remove any obstacle from the mouth that might block the airway
Give mouth-to-mouth resuscitation if he is conscious
Make sure the airway is open and the head is tilted back
questions.explanation:
Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation should only be performed if the person is unconscious and not breathing.

 If the person is conscious, it is dangerous and unnecessary, so it is strictly prohibited.

questions.questionText: In the diagram showing blood circulation system in the human body, the parts indicated by numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4 are respectively:
options: Pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein, vena cava, aorta
Aorta, vena cava, pulmonary vein, pulmonary artery
Vena cava, pulmonary artery, aorta, pulmonary vein
Pulmonary vein, aorta, vena cava, pulmonary artery
questions.explanation:
Blood leaves the left ventricle through the aorta to the body, returns via the vena cava, goes to the lungs through the pulmonary artery, and returns oxygenated via the pulmonary vein.

 Therefore, the correct order is: aorta → vena cava → pulmonary vein → pulmonary artery.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about the activities of the heart?
options: Diastole is when the heart muscles contract and force the blood out.
Systole is when the heart muscles relax and it fills with blood.
The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
As the heart beats blood travels through the arteries with a uniform pressure.
questions.explanation: The 'lub-dub' sound of the heartbeat heard through a stethoscope is produced by the closing of heart valves — the 'lub' is due to atrioventricular valves closing, and the 'dub' due to semilunar valves closing.

questions.questionText: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are important EXCEPT:
options: sterilizing the inoculating loops.
transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.
tilting the lid of the  Petri dish during inoculation.
adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
questions.explanation:
Sterilizing inoculating loops, transferring microorganisms into agar, and slightly tilting the Petri dish lid during inoculation are important aseptic techniques.

 However, adding distilled water to already sterilized agar is unnecessary and may introduce contamination.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases can be caused by more than one type of microorganism?
options: Typhoid
Tuberculosis
Cholera
Gastroenteritis
questions.explanation:
Gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines) is a general syndrome that can be caused by various pathogens, including different bacteria (like Salmonella or E. coli), viruses (like Rotavirus), or parasites.

 The other options are typically caused by a specific microorganism (Typhoid by Salmonella typhi, Tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Cholera by Vibrio cholerae).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases is correctly explained with its causes or symptoms?
options: Gonorrhoea is caused by Treponema pallidum.
Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.
Syphilis is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Gonorrhoea has a burning sensation symptom while urinating.
questions.explanation:
Gonorrhoea is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and a key symptom is often a painful or burning sensation while urinating (dysuria).

 Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, and while it causes a sore (chancre), the first option incorrectly matches the cause of Gonorrhoea with Syphilis.

questions.questionText: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?
options: The highest and the lowest unit of classification
The two highest units of classification
The two lowest units of classification
The two middle units of classification
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, the two-part naming system for organisms, uses the Genus and the Species names, which are the two most specific and therefore the two lowest units of the standard taxonomic hierarchy (Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> **Genus** -> Species).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following phyla is characterized by a flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure, that runs along the dorsal side of the body?
options: Phylum Annelida
Phylum Arthropoda
Phylum Mollusca
Phylum Chordata
questions.explanation: The flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure described is the notochord, which is a defining feature of the phylum Chordata.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?
options: Snail - Phylum Annelida
Earthworm - Phylum Mollusca
Starfish - Phylum Echinodermata
Fish - Phylum Arthropoda
questions.explanation:
Starfish belong to the phylum Echinodermata (spiny-skinned animals).

 Snail belongs to Mollusca, Earthworm to Annelida, and Fish to Chordata.

questions.questionText:
A zoologist studied 5 vertebrate species (spA, spB, spC, spD and spE) and described their features as follows: 

spA: Smooth moist skin; pass parts of their lives in water and on land. 

spB: streamlined body with scales; gills for gaseous exchange.

 spC: feathers over the body with scales on legs; endothermic; horny beak.

 spD: Dry skin covered by scales; lungs for respiration.

 spE: mammary glands; endothermic; high internal body temperature.

 Based on the features listed above, spA, spB, spC, spD and spE can be classified under the vertebrate classes respectively:
options: Pisces, Amphibia, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia, and Pisces.
Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, Mammalia, and Amphibia.
questions.explanation:
Based on the features:

- spA: smooth, moist skin; lives in water and on land → Amphibia

- spB: streamlined body, scales, gills → Pisces (fish)

- spC: feathers, beak, endothermic → Aves (birds)

- spD: dry scaly skin, lungs → Reptilia (reptiles)

- spE: mammary glands, endothermic → Mammalia (mammals)

questions.questionText: Which one of the following events happens during carbon cycle? Carbon dioxide is:
options: removed from the air by animals during respiration.
returned into the air by plants during photosynthesis.
transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
absorbed from air when microbes decompose plant and animals.
questions.explanation:
In the carbon cycle, carbon is fixed into organic molecules by plants (photosynthesis).

 This organic carbon is then transferred from plants to animals when the animals consume them (feeding relationship).

questions.questionText: Which of the following plant adaptation mechanisms helps cactus to adapt in the desert environment?
options: Having broad leaves.
Storing water in its tissue.
Spreading its seeds in wider areas.
Increasing number of stomata in its leaves.
questions.explanation: Cacti are succulents; their primary adaptation to the arid desert is the ability to store large amounts of water in their fleshy stem tissues.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the traditional use of biotechnology's production of:
options: dairy products at household level.
insulin using transgenic bacteria.
vinger using industrial fermenter.
myco-proteins under a laboratory.
questions.explanation:
Traditional biotechnology involves the use of natural organisms and simple techniques to produce products like yogurt, cheese, and other fermented foods at home or small-scale settings.

 The other options involve modern or industrial biotechnology.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis? It:
options: produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.
is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.
produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.
is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the process by which somatic (body) cells divide to produce two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell and contain the full (diploid) chromosome number.

questions.questionText: Consider the following diagram demonstrating the pyramid of energy. Which of the following is INCORRECT about the above pyramid of energy?
options: The organisms of the first trophic level convert light energy into chemical energy.
The organisms of each trophic level use large proportion of the energy to build their body.
The amount of energy transferred through the trophic levels drops with each step up of the pyramid.
The energy lost as heat to the surrounding in each trophic level is insignificant.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: A cross between pea plants having heterozygous genotype (Rr) has been made. Which of the following is correct about the offspring according to the Mendelian inheritance? The genotypic probability of getting
options: RR is 50%.
rr is 25%.
Rr is 25%.
RR is 75%.
questions.explanation: A cross between two heterozygous pea plants (Rr × Rr) produces the following genotypes in a Punnett square: Thus, the probability of offspring being homozygous recessive (rr) is 25%.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about DNA? It is
options: single stranded molecule.
less stable and degrades quickly.
smaller molecule and coding for only protein.
made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
questions.explanation:
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is a polymer made up of monomers called nucleotides.

 Each nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a nitrogenous base (A, T, C, or G).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?
options: RR x Rr
Rr x Rr
RR x RR
RR x rr
questions.explanation:
A test cross is always performed by crossing an organism with an unknown genotype (usually dominant phenotype) with an organism that is homozygous recessive (rr).

 This allows a scientist to determine the genotype of the first organism.
 Among the options, RR x rr (crossing a homozygous dominant with a homozygous recessive) is a type of cross used in Mendelian genetics and fits the definition of crossing with the recessive parent (though Rr x rr is the most common test cross).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is different from the rest with regard to conservation of vegatation?
options: Replanting of land with endemic species
Using local practices for conservation
Large scale introduction of exotic plants
Replanting indigenous tree species
questions.explanation:
Conservation aims to protect native biodiversity. 
Large scale introduction of exotic plants (non-native species) is typically harmful to native ecosystems, as exotic species can outcompete indigenous species, making it the action that is different from accepted conservation practices.

questions.questionText: In the nervous co-ordination system, which of the following statements explains the synapse? It is a:
options: part of the skull that encloses brain for the purpose of protection.
chemical that transmits nerve impulse across the nervous system.
short term change in the electrical potential on the surface of cells.
junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction where a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to another neuron or from a neuron to a muscle cell, allowing communication within the nervous system.

questions.questionText: Two students want to demonstrate a simple spinal reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. One of them sits down with one leg loosely crossed over the other. The other hits the crossed leg just below the knee cap Gentle but  firmly using the edge of his hand. Which one of the following situations will happen during this demonstration? The:
options: hip ligament stretches the muscle
impulse travels to the brain.
impulse travels to quadriceps muscle from the brain.
lower leg will jerk downwards and inwards.
questions.explanation:
In the knee-jerk reflex (a simple spinal reflex), tapping the tendon below the kneecap stretches the quadriceps muscle.

 This stretch is detected by sensory neurons, which send an impulse to the spinal cord. The spinal cord immediately sends a motor impulse back to the quadriceps, causing the lower leg to jerk downwards and slightly inwards without involving the brain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following eye structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Pupil - serves as the eye's protective outer layer.
Choroid - bends the light into the eye.
Cornea - provides nutrition to the retina.
questions.explanation: The Iris contains muscles that constrict or dilate the pupil, thereby controlling the amount of light that enters the eye and reaches the retina.

questions.questionText: What is the function of dermis of the skin? It:
options: forms a waterproof around the body tissue.
contains blood vessels and sweat glands.
acts as protection against heat loss.
protects the entry of pathogens into the body.
questions.explanation: The dermis is the second layer of skin, characterized by a dense matrix of connective tissue that houses structures like blood vessels, hair follicles, and sweat glands.

questions.questionText: Children who play by spinning round and round fast, when they stop, they feel dizzy. Why?
options: The fluid in their semicircular canals keeps on moving after they stop.
The sensory hairs vibrate highly in response to movement of their body.
The otoliths round in the same direction with the head.
The optic nerves reports that the children are still moving.
questions.explanation:
Dizziness after spinning is caused by inertia affecting the endolymph fluid in the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

 When the body stops, the fluid continues to move for a moment, sending signals to the brain that the head is still rotating, leading to the sensation of dizziness.

questions.questionText: When does menstruation start in women with no obvious reproductive a health problem? It happens when
options: pregnancy occurs and the embryo obtains nourishment and oxygen.
the spongy lining of the uterus detaches in the absence of pregnancy.
the fertilized ovum reaches the uterus and attaches into the thick, spongy lining.
the FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary and the egg ripens.
questions.explanation:
Menstruation is the shedding of the thickened inner lining of the uterus (endometrium/spongy lining).

 This occurs specifically when there is no pregnancy, causing a drop in progesterone and estrogen, which triggers the detachment of the lining.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correctly matched with the function of kidney structures?
options: Glomerulus - concentrates urine and conserves water
Loop of Henle - involved in ultrafiltration
Bowman's capsule - acts as a filter to produce urine
Cortex - monitors the osmotic pressure of the blood
questions.explanation: The Bowman's capsule surrounds the glomerulus and collects the fluid forced out of the blood, acting as the initial filter to produce urine (filtrate).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following temperature controlling mechanisms in homotherms is categorized into behavioral method?
options: Shivering as a result of drop in temperature
Seeking shade when the temperature rises
Sweating when the temperature increases
Constriction of capillaries when the temperature falls
questions.explanation:
Behavioral mechanisms involve voluntary actions.

 Seeking shade is a voluntary action used to reduce heat gain and thus control body temperature, classifying it as a behavioral mechanism. 

The other options (A, C, D) are physiological (involuntary) responses.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the liver?
options: Storing glycogen
Controlling cholesterol
Bile formation
Monosaccharide metabolism
questions.explanation:
The liver functions include storing glycogen, controlling cholesterol levels, and forming bile.

 However, monosaccharide metabolism primarily occurs in the cells of the body (e.g., glycolysis in cytoplasm) rather than being a direct function of the liver.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following leaf structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Waxy cuticle - controls the entry of carbon dioxide into the leaf
Palisade mesophyll - the main photosynthetic tissue of the leaf
Spongy mesophyll - helps to prevent water loss from the leaf
Guard cells - have lots of air space and gas exchange area of the leaf
questions.explanation:
The Palisade mesophyll is the layer of cells just below the epidermis.

 Its cells are tightly packed and contain a high concentration of chloroplasts, making it the main site of photosynthesis in the leaf. 

The waxy cuticle prevents water loss; guard cells control gas exchange; and spongy mesophyll allows gas movement.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the movement of materials in plants?
options: The transport of organic materials is due to transpiration.
Passive transport can take place in the pholem.
Active transport can take place in the xylem.
Water is transported in dead tissue.
questions.explanation:
Water is transported through the xylem vessels, which are composed of dead tissue (tracheids and vessel elements).

 Organic materials (sugars) are transported in the phloem, and their movement is active, not passive, and not primarily driven by transpiration (which drives water movement in the xylem).

questions.questionText: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant? The:
options: stem will grow.
leaves will fall.
side shoots will grow fast.
roots will storages.
questions.explanation:
Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation and cell division.

When an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant, the hormone stimulates stem growth, making the plant taller.

The other options (leaf fall, side shoot growth, root storage) are not primary effects of gibberellins.

questions.questionText:
A biologist collected two types of seeds (SA and SB) from the field and sowed them in moist soils enriched with nutrients. Then, he recorded his observations as follows:

 SA
     The seedling of this seed emerged from the soil curved while pushing up through the soil.

 The hypocotyl straightened and carried the cotyledons and plumule above the soil surface.

 SB
     The plumule of the seedling pushed its way out of the soil, while the cotyledon remained underground.

     Unlike what occurred during the germination of SA, the plumule of this seed did not form a hook.

Which one of the following is correct about the observations of the biologist?
options: SA is of a monocot, while SB is of a dicot.
Both SA and SB are of monocots.
SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
Both SA and SB are of dicots.
questions.explanation:
The observations describe two types of germination:

SA shows epigeal germination (cotyledons pulled above ground by the lengthening hypocotyl hook).
 This type of germination is typical of dicots (Dicotyledons).

SB shows hypogeal germination (plumule pushes straight out while cotyledons remain underground).

 This type is typical of monocots (Monocotyledons).

Therefore, SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an Ethiopian endemic plant?
options: Bahir zaf
Bunna
Noug seed
Avocado
questions.explanation:
Noug (Guizotia abyssinica) is endemic to Ethiopia, meaning it naturally grows only in this region.

 The other plants—Bunna (coffee), Bahir zaf, and Avocado—are found in multiple regions outside Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in
options: Bale Mountain National Park.
Simien Mountains National Park.
Nechisar National Park.
Omo National Park.
questions.explanation: The Walia Ibex (Capra walie) is an endemic and critically endangered wild goat species found almost exclusively in the Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: All of the following sentences are correct about pollution EXCEPT
options: burning fossil fuels increases pollution due to the release of hydrocarbons.
burning of wood increases pollution by causing global dimming which blocks sunlight.
deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed from the atmosphere.
decomposition of dead bodies increases the amount of CO₂ in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation:
The statement that deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed** is INCORRECT.

 Deforestation *decreases* the absorption of CO2 (because trees are carbon sinks), leading to a net *ncrease of CO2 in the atmosphere, which contributes to pollution (global warming).

questions.questionText: When a biologist shares her research findings with other fellow biologists, she is
options: drawing her conclusion.
analyzing her data.
making her hypothesis.
reporting her result.
questions.explanation: Sharing findings (often through publication or presentation) is the final stage of the scientific method, where the scientist is reporting her result to the scientific community.

questions.questionText:
A student conducted an experiment using different enzymes to assess the enhancement of reaction rates under different conditions. She represents her results as indicated in the following table:

Which one of the following is an acceptable conclusion of the experiment?
options: The rate enhancement for enzymes 'Z' is less because it didn't use a cofactor.
The temperature increases the rate of chemical reaction decreases.
Enzyme 'Y' should be enhanced the rate better at temperature slightly higher than 37°C.
Enzyme 'M' cannot enhance the rate of reaction further if the temperature exceeds 30°C.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences correctly describes the properties of water? It:
options: allows all light wavelengths to pass through its various depths.
requires high amount of energy to heat up.
contracts when it freezes and hence acts as an insulator.
takes low energy to change into vapor.
questions.explanation:
Water has a very high specific heat capacity. This means it requires a high amount of energy to heat up (or change its temperature).

 The high specific heat helps moderate temperatures on Earth.

questions.questionText: An organic molecule which is an important part of structure of chromosome is
options: amylose.
triglyceride.
amino acid.
glycogen.
questions.explanation:
Chromosomes are primarily composed of DNA and proteins (histones).

 Proteins are polymers made up of amino acids. Amylose and glycogen are carbohydrates, and triglyceride is a lipid.

questions.questionText: In animal cells, glycogen is hydrolyzed quickly to release glucose for respiration. This is due to the presence of several
options: β-1,4-glycosidic bonds.
enzymes that hydrolyze it easily.
microfibrils in its side chain.
(α)-1,6- glycosidic bonds.
questions.explanation:
Glycogen is the storage form of glucose in animals.

 It is highly branched, featuring both alpha-1,4 and many alpha(α)-1,6-glycosidic bonds. 
This high degree of branching provides many free ends (non-reducing ends) where enzymes can simultaneously hydrolyze the glucose units, allowing for the quick release of glucose for respiration.

questions.questionText:
This question is based on the following diagram which depicts structural formula of a biological molecule.

The molecule represented by the above structure is
options: fatty acid.
glycerol.
cellulose.
amylopectin.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Industries in the medicine sector use glucose oxidase in Clinistix strips for
options: easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
reducing the viscosity of mucus.
restoring blood supply to areas of heart muscle.
detecting toxic metabolites in the blood.
questions.explanation:
Glucose oxidase is an enzyme used in Clinistix strips to detect glucose in urine.

 High glucose levels in urine indicate hyperglycemia, which helps in the diagnosis of diabetes.

questions.questionText: In the systematic naming of enzymes, assume an enzyme is designated as EC 3.4.11.1. Which of the following correctly describes this enzyme?
options: 4 - shows to which main class the enzyme belongs.
3 - indicates a subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
11 - gives a sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
1 - a reference of its enzyme commission.
questions.explanation:
The Enzyme Commission (EC) number is a numerical classification system for enzymes.
 The four numbers represent a hierarchy: Class.Subclass.Sub-subclass.Serial Number.
 The first digit, 3, indicates the main enzyme class (in this case, 'Hydrolases').
 The subsequent numbers define the reaction with increasing specificity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the lock-and-key model of enzyme action? The
options: shape of the substrate is complementary to the active site.
attachment of substrate to an enzyme produces a conformational change.
attached substrate- the enzyme complex enters into a transition state.
model explains enzyme inhibition in a complete manner.
questions.explanation:
The lock-and-key model (proposed by Emil Fischer) posits that the active site of an enzyme is a rigid structure perfectly shaped to fit only one specific substrate, much like a lock and key. This is described as a complementary shape.

 Option B describes the 'Induced-Fit' model, which is a more modern refinement.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about apo-enzymes? They are
options: organic  molecules and many are derived from vitamins.
inorganic molecules that bind loosely with the cofactors.
cofactors that give an enzyme its catalytic activity.
proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.
questions.explanation:
An apo-enzyme is the inactive protein part of an enzyme.
 It becomes a functional, active enzyme (called a holoenzyme) only when it combines with a non-protein component called a cofactor (or coenzyme). 
Therefore, apo-enzymes are proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.

questions.questionText: How does a competitive inhibitor affect an enzyme catalyzed reaction? By
options: blocking the allosteric site of the enzyme.
blocking the active site of the enzyme.
denaturing the active site of the enzyme.
producing conformational change of the enzyme.
questions.explanation:
A competitive inhibitor is a molecule that is structurally similar to the substrate.
 It competes directly with the substrate for binding to the enzyme's active site. 

By binding to the active site, it prevents the actual substrate from binding, thus blocking the active site of the enzyme and reducing the reaction rate.

questions.questionText: In a metabolic pathway, the end-product inhibition occurs when the
options: first product of the pathway inhibits the last enzymatic reaction.
last product of the pathway inhibits the last enzymatic reaction.
last product of the pathway inhibits the first enzymatic reaction.
first product of the pathway inhibits the third enzyme of the reaction.
questions.explanation:
End-product inhibition (or feedback inhibition) is a regulatory mechanism in metabolism where the accumulation of the final product of a sequence of reactions inhibits the enzyme that catalyzes the first committed step (often the first enzyme) of that pathway.

 This prevents unnecessary overproduction of the final product, thus the last product of the pathway inhibits the first enzymatic reaction.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the description of the cell theory?
options: Virchow stated that cell is the unit of structure, physiology and reproduction of living things.
Schleiden and Schwann stated that all cells come from pre-existing cells.
spontaneous generation theory states that all cells have basically different chemical composition.
Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information that passes from cell to cell.
questions.explanation:
The Modern Cell Theory incorporates the original tenets and adds that cells carry hereditary information (DNA) which is passed from the parent cell to the daughter cells during division.

 Option A incorrectly attributes the combination of structure, physiology, and reproduction to Virchow (he primarily contributed the idea that cells come from pre-existing cells).

 Option B describes Virchow's contribution, not Schleiden and Schwann's original part.

 Option C is entirely incorrect as the spontaneous generation theory was disproved.

questions.questionText: A student measured the diameter of onion epidermal cells at a magnification of 100X using a field of view adjusted to 2mm by stage micrometer. What would be the diameter of individual cells if 8 cells fit into the field of view of the microscope at 100X magnification?
options: 200μm
250μm
300μm
150μm
questions.explanation: The diameter of a cell is calculated by dividing the field of view by the number of cells fitting into it: 2000 μm ÷ 8 = 250 μm.

questions.questionText: Which of the following characteristics of cells is found only in prokaryotic cell?
options: Continuous loop of DNA
Division of labor within the cell
Higher level of complexity
10 - 100 μm long
questions.explanation:
Prokaryotic cells have their genetic material in the form of a single circular (continuous loop) DNA molecule, unlike eukaryotic cells which have linear chromosomes.

 The other options—division of labor, higher complexity, and large size—are features of eukaryotic cells.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions of proteins is correctly matched with its function in a cell membrane?
options: Glycoprotein - reduces the fluidity of the membrane
Peripheral protein - anchor integral proteins to the cytoskeleton
Carrier proteins - specific ions can pass along them
Channel proteins - larger molecules can pass through them
questions.explanation:
Carrier proteins bind specifically to a substance (like glucose, amino acids, or specific ions) on one side of the membrane, change their conformation (shape), and release the substance on the other side.

 Option A is incorrect; cholesterol controls fluidity.

 Option B is incorrect; integral proteins attach to the cytoskeleton, and peripheral proteins are only loosely attached. 

Option D is incorrect; channel proteins allow small ions/water to pass, while carrier proteins or other mechanisms transport larger molecules.

questions.questionText: In the aerobic cellular respiration
options: glycolysis takes place in the mitochondria.
Krebs cycle takes place in the cytoplasm.
pyruvate enters into the mitochondria for further stages.
electron transport chain takes place in the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation:
Cellular respiration begins with glycolysis in the cytoplasm, which produces pyruvate.

 In aerobic respiration, the pyruvate is then actively transported into the mitochondria (specifically the matrix) where it is converted to acetyl-CoA, which then enters the Krebs cycle.

 Options A, B, and D incorrectly place the stages; glycolysis is in the cytoplasm, Krebs cycle is in the mitochondrial matrix, and the electron transport chain is on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.questionText: Suppose a hypothetical cell of 15% solute concentration is put in a beaker containing 90% water and 10% solute. In which way will the water move?
options: From the cell to the beaker
From the beaker to the cell
Both into and out of the cell
Both into and out of the beaker
questions.explanation:
Water moves by osmosis from a region of higher water potential (lower solute concentration) to a region of lower water potential (higher solute concentration).

 The beaker (90% water) has a higher water potential than the cell (85% water), so water moves from the beaker to the cell.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about transport of substances across the cell membrane?
options: Facilitated diffusion - particles move from high water potential to lower one.
Simple diffusion - large particles transported through channel proteins .
Active transport - particles move from low to higher concentration using carrier protein .
Passive transport - particles require energy in the form of ATP to derive the transport.
questions.explanation:
Active transport requires energy (ATP) to move substances against their concentration gradient, meaning from a region of low to high concentration, typically utilizing specialized protein carriers (pumps). Option A describes osmosis.

 Option B is partially true, but facilitated diffusion is for movement down the concentration gradient.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following processes of aerobic respiration takes place in the Krebs cycle?
options: Two molecules of ATP are used to phosphorylate each molecule of glucose.
Hydrogen atoms carried by reduced NAD and FAD are released and split into  protons and electrons.
Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is split into two molecules of the three-carbon sugar GP.
Two carbon group from acetyl coenzyme A reacts with a 4-carbon compound to form citrate.
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle (or Citric Acid Cycle) is initiated when the two-carbon acetyl group from acetyl-CoA combines with the four-carbon compound oxaloacetate to form the six-carbon molecule **citrate**. Options A and C are part of glycolysis. Option B is part of the electron transport chain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following processes takes place when lactate is produced?
options: ATP is produced through oxidative phosphorylation.
NAD and FAD are regenerated from reduced NAD and FAD.
Reduced NAD supplies oxygen and becomes oxidized itself.
Protons accumulation created in the inter-membrane space.
questions.explanation:
Lactate production occurs during anaerobic fermentation.
 The primary purpose of this reaction is to regenerate NAD+ from NADH (reduced NAD) so that glycolysis can continue. 

Therefore, NAD is regenerated from reduced NAD. While FAD is not directly involved, the overall process is accurately described by the regeneration of the oxidized electron carrier.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following structures of the photosystem is correctly related with its function?
options: Antenna complex - light-dependent reaction begins
Chlorophyll a - a reaction center molecule
Thylakoid - absorbs blue and red pigments
Carotenoid - provides the hydrogen ions
questions.explanation:
Within a photosystem, a specialized pair of Chlorophyll a molecules reside at the reaction center. 
They are responsible for absorbing light energy and initiating the electron transport chain, acting as the primary electron donor.

questions.questionText: What happens during the electron transport system of respiration? The
options: hydrogen atoms carried by FADH and NADH are released and split into protons and electrons
four-carbon compound undergoes molecular transformation to generate oxaloacetate
Five carbon compound is further decarboxylated to form a four-carbon compound.
Citrate losses a carbon atom to form a five-carbon atom compound and CO2.
questions.explanation:
During the electron transport system (ETS) of respiration, NADH and FADH2 donate hydrogen atoms, which are split into protons (H⁺) and electrons (e⁻).

 The electrons move through the electron transport chain, driving the production of ATP, while protons contribute to the proton gradient used in chemiosmosis.

questions.questionText: During light-independent reactions of photosynthesis, glucose is synthesized through...
options: six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one molecule of glucose.
synthesis of reduced NADP and release of hydrogen ion.
transmission of electrons to the inside of the thylakoid.
release of hydrogen ions at the electron transport chain.
questions.explanation:
The light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) use ATP and NADPH generated from the light reactions to convert CO2 into sugar. 
The cycle must turn **six times (fix 6 CO2 molecules) to produce the net yield of one molecule of the six-carbon sugar glucose (C6H12O6.
 Options B, C, and D describe events in the light-dependent reactions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following factors of photosynthesis is correctly matched with its effect?
options: Low temperature - limits the rate of reactions by reducing the number of electrons in the chlorophyll.
CO2 concentration - limits the reactions by influencing rate of initial reactions with RuBP.
Light intensity - limits the rate of ATP synthase enzyme action in light dependent reactions.
Low RuBisCO - limits the number of reactions in the light dependent reaction.
questions.explanation:
Carbon dioxide concentration is a major limiting factor for photosynthesis because CO2 is the substrate for the enzyme RuBisCO in the Calvin cycle.
 Thus, CO2 concentration limits the rate of the initial CO2 fixation reaction with the five-carbon acceptor, RuBP (Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate).

questions.questionText: In the CAM photosynthetic pathway,
options: glucose is synthesized in the bundle sheath cell during night.
malate is stored in the mesophyll cells during the day.
the C4 stage and the Calvin cycle are separated in time.
ATP and NADPH are produced during the night.
questions.explanation:
The CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) pathway is an adaptation to arid environments.
 CO2 is initially fixed into an organic acid (like malate) at night (C4 stage) and then released to the Calvin cycle during the day. This separates the two stages in time, which minimizes water loss. Option B is reversed: malate is stored at night and broken down during the day. Options A and D are incorrect.

questions.questionText: In Gram staining, if some bacteria retain the crystal violet after counter staining, then the bacteria is
options: Gram negative.
Gram positive.
Gram intermediate.
Gram variable.
questions.explanation:
The key feature of a Gram-positive bacterium is its thick peptidoglycan cell wall, which retains the initial stain, crystal violet, even after the decolorization step.

 Therefore, when counter-stained with safranin, these bacteria still appear purple/violet (retain the crystal violet).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the mechanism of bacterium to produce disease?
options: It enters into the living cells and disrupts the metabolic system.
It hyphae secrets enzymes which digest substances of the tissue.
Its genetic material is incorporated into the cell for instruction.
It attaches with white blood cells and destroy the immune system.
questions.explanation: (It enters into the living cells and disrupts the metabolic system) is closer to bacterial action for pathogenic bacteria.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the role of bacteria in genetic engineering? They are used to
options: open up a plasmid
isolate genes from donor DNA.
contain a recombinant plasmid.
cut genes from donor DNA.
questions.explanation:
In genetic engineering, bacteria (specifically E. colis) are used as host cells for cloning. A recombinant plasmid (a small circular DNA molecule containing the gene of interest) is inserted into the bacterium, which then replicates the plasmid, effectively containing a recombinant plasmid and multiplying the desired gene.

 Option A, B, and D are steps carried out by enzymes (like restriction enzymes and ligase) in vitro (in a test tube).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences describes a virus?
options: is saprophyte.
has differentiated organelles.
undergoes respiration.
is acellular.
questions.explanation:
A virus is an acellular particle (not a cell) consisting of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat.
 They are obligate intracellular parasites that lack the necessary machinery for metabolism or respiration. Therefore, the most accurate description is that it is not cellular.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is true about viruses?
options: Corona virus is a DNA virus.
AIDS caused by a DNA virus.
Herpes simplex is a DNA virus.
Swine flu is caused by an RNA virus.
questions.explanation:
The Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), which causes cold sores and genital herpes, is a type of DNA virus.

 Corona viruses and Swine flu are RNA viruses. AIDS is caused by HIV, which is an RNA retrovirus.

questions.questionText:
The following steps are involved when HIV infects its host cell in the human body.

1. Conversion of viral RNA into DNA and its incorporation into cell's DNA.

2. Viral DNA's transcription into viral RNA and production of proteins.
3. Assemblage of new viral particles from RNA, proteins and Reverse Transcriptase.

4. The binding of gp120 of HIV to CD4 of a T-Lymphocyte.

5. Fusion of HIV with the plasma membrane of the host cell.

6. Release of the RNA and reverse transcriptase into the cell.

The logical order of the steps listed above would be:
questions.explanation:
HIV infection begins when gp120 binds to the CD4 receptor (4), followed by fusion with the host cell membrane (5).
 The viral RNA and reverse transcriptase are released into the cell (6). 
Reverse transcription converts viral RNA into DNA and integrates it into the host genome (1). 
The viral DNA is then transcribed and translated to produce viral RNA and proteins (2), and finally new viral particles are assembled (3).

questions.questionText: This item is based on the following diagram which depicts the water cycle. In the above diagram, the letters A,B, C and D respectively represent
options: evaporation, precipitation, transpiration, condensation.
evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation.
evaporation, precipitation, condensation, transpiration.
evaporation, transpiration, precipitation, condensation.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following bacteria produces ammonium ion by forming a symbiotic association with peas and beans?
options: Azotobacter
Klebsiella
Rhizobium
Pseudomonas
questions.explanation:
Rhizobium bacteria form a mutualistic (symbiotic) relationship with leguminous plants like peas and beans (pulses).

 These bacteria live in root nodules where they perform nitrogen fixation, converting atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonium ions (NH4+), which the plant can use.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following comparisons is true about primary and secondary succession? Secondary succession has
options: reduced total biomass of the community
Reduced species diversity.
More stable community.
has slower progress to reach the climax.
questions.explanation:
In secondary succession, the area already has soil and perhaps existing seed banks and roots, meaning the starting biomass is not zero (unlike primary succession).

 Therefore, it typically has a reduced total biomass compared to the eventual climax community because it starts from a disturbed, non-climax state. Alternatively, secondary succession is generally faster (Option D is wrong), and while it has fewer initial species, the final community is equally stable (Option C is wrong).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences describes the tropical rainforest biome? It has
options: sparse - succulent plants.
migrating animals.
poor and thin soil.
frozen and rocky soil.
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests** have **poor and thin soil (or lateritic soil). This is because the high rainfall rapidly washes away nutrients (leaching), and decomposition happens so quickly that nutrients are immediately taken up by the dense vegetation, leaving very little in the topsoil. Option A describes a desert. Option B describes biomes like the savanna or tundra. Option D describes the tundra.

questions.questionText: Fresh water biomes like streams and rivers are characterized by the presence of
options: algae, planktons and fish.
corals, crabs and planktons.
angler fish, algae and crabs.
corals, kelps and angler fish.
questions.explanation:
Freshwater biomes are characterized by organisms adapted to flowing water, including photosynthetic organisms like algae, floating organisms like plankton (phyto- and zoo-), and various species of fish.
 Corals, crabs, kelp, and angler fish are typically found in marine (saltwater) environments.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes intra-specific and inter-specific competition? In intra-specific competition the
options: competition is for a few requirements but in inter-specific competition the competition is for all requirements.
competition is less severe but in inter-specific competition it is more.
competing individuals belong to different species but in inter-specific competition the individuals are of the same species.
competing individuals have similar adaptation but in inter-specific competition the adaptation is different.
questions.explanation:
Intra-specific competition (competition within the same species) is often less severe than inter-specific competition (competition between different species).

 This is because different species competing for the same limited resources often exploit those resources differently, leading to a more acute struggle.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following stages of cell division is correctly described in meiosis II?
options: Anaphase II - chromatids from each chromosome separate
Prophase II - pairs of homologous chromosomes split up
Telophase II - two haploid cells are produced
Metaphase II - chromosomes pair and exchange segments
questions.explanation: Meiosis II separates sister chromatids. During **Anaphase II, the chromatids that make up each chromosome separate and move to opposite poles, becoming individual chromosomes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following events is an example of a sex-influenced trait?
options: Lactation
Pattern baldness
Un-descended testicles
Retinitis pigmentosa
questions.explanation:
A sex-influenced trait is an autosomal trait whose expression is dictated by the sex of the individual, often due to hormonal differences.
 Pattern baldness** is the classic example, as the gene acts as dominant in males but recessive in females.

questions.questionText: In a dihybrid self-crossing of a plant with genotype DdCc, 3600 offspring were produced. How many of the offspring will have the ddcc genotype?
questions.explanation:
In a dihybrid self-cross (DdCc × DdCc), the genotypic ratio follows 1:2:1 for each gene.
 The probability of dd is 1/4 and the probability of cc is 1/4.
 Since the genes assort independently, the probability of ddcc is (1/4 × 1/4) = 1/16.

 Therefore, 1/16 of 3600 = 225 offspring.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement regarding translation in eukaryotic cells. The
options: polymerase assembles free RNA nucleotides into a chain.
helicase enzyme begins to unwind a section of DNA.
RNA polymerase moves along the antisense strand.
First two codons of the mRNA enter the ribosome.
questions.explanation:
Translation is the process where a ribosome reads mRNA to synthesize a protein.
 The ribosome starts by positioning the mRNA so that the first two codons are ready to be read and bind the corresponding transfer RNA (tRNA) molecules.
 Options A, B, and C describe transcription or DNA replication.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains how crossing over brings variation?
options: In meiosis I, there is exchange of a section of DNA between chromatids
In meiosis I there is splitting up of pairs of homologous chromosomes and line up.
In meiosis II, chromatids from each chromosome are separated at random
In meiosis II, homologous chromosomes align themselves independent of other pairs
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis I, where homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange corresponding segments of DNA between non-sister chromatids. This exchange creates new combinations of alleles, leading to genetic variation.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following model of DNA replication.

Which one of the following is true about A, B and C?
options: is not identical with A and B.
and B are identical with each other but not with C.
A, B and C are not identical with each other.
and C are not identical with each other.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: What is the central role of tRNA in translation?
options: Recognizing the codon of mRNA and bring the correct amino acid to the ribosomes
Carrying genetic information from DNA in the nucleus to ribosomes
Assembling the amino acid into a polypeptide chain
Acting as a template for converting a genetic code into amino acid sequence
questions.explanation: The role of transfer RNA (tRNA) is to match its anticodon to the mRNA codon, thereby ensuring the correct amino acid is brought to the ribosome for protein synthesis.

questions.questionText: Sickle cell anemia is caused by the replacement of glutamic acid by valine at a specific position in the beta chains of hemoglobin. This change is an example of which mutation?
options: Substitution
Addition
Deletion
Inversion
questions.explanation: The replacement of one nucleotide base with another in the DNA sequence, which leads to the substitution of one amino acid (glutamic acid) for another (valine) in the protein, is called a Substitution mutation.

questions.questionText: Stanley Miller conducted spark-discharge experiment by taking a mixture of gases that he thought to represent the primitive atmosphere of the Earth. All of the following were found in his gas mixture EXCEPT
options: CH4
NH3
CO2
H2
questions.explanation: The Miller-Urey experiment simulated a reducing atmosphere which included methane (CH4), ammonia (NH3), hydrogen (H2), and water vapor, but notably excluded or had very little carbon dioxide (CO2) or free oxygen (O2).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the Darwin theory of evolution?
options: There is a natural variation in features that are heritable.
Environment changes, creating a need for organism to change.
There is development of new feature to order to survive.
New features acquired in lifetime are passed to the offspring.
questions.explanation: A central tenet of Darwin's theory of Natural Selection is the existence of natural, heritable variation within a population, which provides the raw material for selection to act upon.

questions.questionText: Comparative anatomy provides evidence of evolution because it
options: has remains of animals and plants from the remote past.
looks at structural similarities of organisms.
studies the development of the embryos of vertebrates.
has an impression of animal even if the actual parts are missing.
questions.explanation:
Comparative anatomy is the study of similarities and differences in structure (morphology) between different species.

 Finding homologous structures, such as the similar bone structure in the limbs of mammals, provides evidence of evolution by demonstrating structural similarities of organisms descending from a common ancestor.

questions.questionText: About 3 million years ago the Isthmus of Panama separated the shrimp population of the Caribbean Sea and created two populations of shrimps, one on either side of the isthmus. They still look remarkably similar, but they do not interbreed with each other. Which type of isolation is described by this scenario?
options: Geographical isolation
Seasonal isolation
Temporal isolation
Behavioural isolation
questions.explanation: The formation of a physical barrier like the Isthmus of Panama, which separates a single population and prevents gene flow, is known as Geographical isolation (allopatric speciation).

questions.questionText: In the course of evolution, which of the following is true about the human brain?
options: Australopithecus have a brain size between 1.8% and 2.3% of their body mass.
Modern humans have a brain size between 0.7% and 1.0% of their body mass.
Homo sapiens brain uses 25% of the resting energy requirement.
The pre-humans brain uses 80% of the resting energy requirement.
questions.explanation: The human brain, while only about 2% of body mass, is highly metabolic and consumes about 20%-25% of the body's total resting energy requirement (Basal Metabolic Rate).

questions.questionText: All of the following are examples of innate behaviours EXCEPT
options: increasing breathing rate during exercise
training killer whales at marine parks
fly moving its maggot into more humid environment.
producing tears when dust gets into the eyes.
questions.explanation:
Innate behaviours are automatic, unlearned responses (reflexes or fixed action patterns) like sucking or breathing.

 The reference to 'tramit kills by whales at marine parks' is highly likely a typo for a learned behavior (like a trained trick or a modified predatory behavior in captivity) which is the exception to innate behaviors.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of in-sight learning?
options: Use of boxes, after several trials , by a chimpanzee placed in an enclosed area to obtain bananas placed on the top of an enclosure.
Salivation of a dog when a bell was rung in the absence of food, which was paired with the conditioned stimulus.
Lack of response from a lady, which sat in a shop in which a strong deodorant was continuously released from a can.
Exhibition of modifications of natural behaviors of guide dogs, horses or zoo animals to desired behaviors.
questions.explanation:
Insight learning is a form of cognitive learning where an animal solves a problem by suddenly understanding the relationships between parts, often without prior trial-and-error.
 The classic experiment involves a chimp using a tool (like stacking boxes to reach food) which is described in option A.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of a learned behaviour?
options: Knee-jerk reflex
Nest-building
Classical conditioning
Weaving a web
questions.explanation:
Classical conditioning is a form of associative learned behaviour where an animal associates a previously neutral stimulus with a biologically significant one.

 The other options are examples of innate or fixed action patterns.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of territorial behaviour of animals?
options: Fixed action of zebra fish to find a mate
male robin threatening an intruder
Honeybees nesting in a tree
Penguins huddling to reduce heat loss
questions.explanation: Territorial behaviour** involves the aggressive defense of a space against rivals of the same species. A male robin threatening an intruder (usually another male) is a typical example of this behavior.
